title: Re-releases of Wing Commander, Ultima titles hit Steam and GOG
gist: EA re-released 25 classic 1990s games, including Wing Commander and most of the Ultima series, on Steam and GOG for $5 or less each, with remasters driven by producer Jim Vessella's largely volunteer cataloging of an archive of original masters. Light consumer/gaming news with modest catalog-monetization signal.

insights.claim: EA placed 25 lightly remastered classic games, including several Wing Commander titles and nearly all Ultima games, on Steam and GOG, none priced above $5.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Low-cost monetization of legacy IP via third-party stores.
insights.locator: Many people are not big fans

insights.claim: Previous owners of the old versions on GOG and the EA storefront receive the remasters for free.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Goodwill-oriented release rather than a major revenue driver.
insights.locator: The e collection is on sale

insights.claim: EA senior producer Jim Vessella found an archive at EA's Redwood Shores campus containing virtually all original masters of Wing Commander III and IV full-motion-video cutscenes.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Physical archives of legacy assets can unlock remaster value.

insights.claim: The remasters add much higher-quality FMV, 60 fps gameplay, new .INI tweaks and controller support, built with community modder Matt Wells and GOG.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.locator: The flagship offering of those remasters

insights.claim: The author argues the project shows a few passionate people can achieve remarkable game preservation, even though much was done on a volunteer basis outside working hours.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Preservation relied on individual initiative, not institutional strategy.
insights.quote: this shows that a few passionate people can do something remarkable for game preservation
